newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sanyo Sec denies report of liquidating affiliates.
newsitem.headline: Sanyo Sec denies report of liquidating affiliates.

text.p: Sanyo Securities Co Ltd on Wednesday denied a newspaper report that it has decided to apply to the court to liquidate some of its affiliates.
The brokerage also denied that it is considering reducing its capital as part of changes in its restructuring plans.

The Nihon Kogyo Shimbun business daily reported on Wednesday that Sanyo Securities has decided to seek liquidation of some of its affiliates, including a nonbank finance firm, because of continuing bad-loan problems at the affiliates.
To help bail out the ailing non-bank financial affiliate, the second-tier brokerage launched a nine-year restructuring programme in the 1994/95 business year.

Sanyo has received subordinated loans from major life insurance companies, such as Nippon Life Insurance Co and Dai-Ichi Mutual Life Insurance Co, in an attempt to increase capital and strengthen its financial status.
Sanyo said on Wednesday that it was asking life insurers for a delay in the repayment of the subordinated loans which come due at the end of July 1998.
Subordinated loans cease to be accounted as capital once the remaining period to maturity falls below one year. At that point, such loans are treated as short-term debt.

The medium-sized brokerage had a total of 20 billion yen in subordinated loans from nine life insurers at the end of March, 1996, including four billion yen from Nippon Life and three billion from Dai-Ichi Mutual, a Sanyo financial report said.
Sanyo was the second biggest percentage loser on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's first section in Wednesday morning trade.
Sanyo's shares ended the morning session at 152 yen, down 17 yen from the previous day's close.
A Nippon Life spokesman told Reuters on Wednesday that the company is still waiting for a new restructuring plan from Sanyo Securities. He did not give further details.
